title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a compactification of the modular multiplicities M_{g,ν} whose boundary D is a divisor with normal crossings (Deligne–Mumford type). Grothendieck wants to describe the 'structure at infinity' combinatorially and analytically.

Notation, reconstructed from this page and the neighbouring ones:
- D_d is the normalized stratum of points of multiplicity ≥ d of D. A point of D_d is a point x together with an unordered choice of d local branches through x.
- D̃_d → D_d is the principal S_d-covering that orders the branches.
- For d > δ, D_{d,δ} is the space of pairs (point of D_d, choice of δ among its d branches). It comes with two maps:
  - D_{d,δ} → D_d, a finite covering (forget the choice);
  - D_{d,δ} → D_δ, the 'boundary morphism' (164): view the deeper point as a point of the shallower normalized stratum.
- The morphisms D_J → D_{J'} indexed by subsets of branches (from page 55) are recovered once the compatibilities (158) and these maps are known.

He interprets D_{d,δ} as the space or multiplicity of 'arrows' (inclusion morphisms) between the sub-multiplicities at infinity associated with D.

(165) For d > d' > d'' there is a canonical isomorphism D_{d,d'} ×_{D_{d'}} D_{d',d''} ≅ D_{d,d',d''}, the space of flags of branch choices d'' ⊂ d' ⊂ d.

(166) From this one gets the evident projections D_{d,d',d''} → D_{d,d'} ⇉ D_d, D_{d'} and D_{d,d',d''} → D_{d',d''} ⇉ D_{d'}, D_{d''}.

(167) The composition map D_{d,d',d''} → D_{d,d''} (forget the middle step) is not given directly by the fibre-product description.

(168) He notes that D_{d,d''} → D_d × D_{d''} is a monomorphism. The next page adds the margin remark that this holds in the context of analytic spaces. Hence (167) is determined by its two components to D_d and D_{d''}.

Next page: this packages into a category object in analytic spaces (the 'infrastructure analytique' of the boundary). Objects are ∐ D_d, arrows are ∐ D_{d,δ} (plus identities), with source and target maps and composition via the fibre product. This internal category is the proposed definition of a 'modular structure at infinity'.
errors: No mathematical error. (165) is correct: a flag of branch choices is exactly a composable pair.
(168) as a monomorphism relies on D_δ being the branch-normalization, so that a point of D_δ remembers its branches. This is true for analytic spaces.

In the stack ('multiplicité') setting, with automorphisms permuting branches, (168) need not be a monomorphism. Composition would then be extra data. The margin remark 'ceci [valable] dans le contexte des espaces analytiques' suggests Grothendieck was aware of this. The gap for orbifold/stack boundaries is not addressed on this page.

ideas.what: Space of incidences D_{d,δ} between normalized multiplicity strata of a normal-crossings divisor, with a covering map to D_d and a boundary map to D_δ
ideas.modern_name: incidence correspondences of boundary strata; branch-normalization of the strata of a normal crossings divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II, 1971, ordered version as a semi-simplicial space); standard in stratification theory

ideas.what: Composition of incidences via the fibre product D_{d,d'} ×_{D_{d'}} D_{d',d''} ≅ D_{d,d',d''}, assembling the boundary into an internal category in analytic spaces (category of strata enriched in spaces)
ideas.modern_name: internal category / category of strata of a normal-crossings compactification; analytic enrichment of the boundary complex (symmetric Δ-complex / generalized cone complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (2015) for the tropical/cone complex of M_{g,n}; Chan–Galatius–Payne (2018–21) for symmetric Δ-complexes; exit-path categories (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower, but not to this internal-category formalism

ideas.what: Determining composition through the monomorphism D_{d,d''} → D_d × D_{d''}, valid for analytic spaces but not for multiplicités/stacks
ideas.modern_name: faithfulness of the source–target map of a category of strata (a 'poset-like' or monomorphic internal category)

missed.claim: Grothendieck encodes the boundary of M_{g,ν} as a category object in analytic spaces. Objects are the normalized strata D_d, with S_d-torsors ordering the branches; arrows are the incidence spaces D_{d,δ}. This is a space-level (analytic) enrichment of what later appears as the symmetric Δ-complex / generalized cone complex boundary structure of M_{g,n} (Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne; Chan–Galatius–Payne), and of Deligne's semi-simplicial normal-crossings resolution in unordered form.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The tropical and boundary-complex literature keeps only the combinatorial shadow, the dual complex. An internal category retaining the analytic strata and covering maps is a natural object for 'tropical + analytic' or stratified-homotopy descriptions of the boundary of M_{g,n}, and Grothendieck's version predates these works.

missed.claim: Grothendieck notes that the determination of composition via the monomorphism (168) works for analytic spaces. Extending it to the stack setting (boundaries of modular multiplicities with automorphisms) would require composition as extra data, i.e. a 2-categorical or stacky internal category. This is not worked out here.
missed.quote: mais non directement (167) D_{d,d',d''} → D_{d,d''}, mais on note que (168) D_{d,d''} → D_d × D_{d''} [est un mono]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the precise point where stacky boundary structures (log stacks, Artin fans, the stack of tropical curves) differ from the coarse picture.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a clean internal-category formalism for the boundary stratification of M_{g,ν}. It anticipates, in analytic-space form, the later boundary-complex and symmetric-Δ-complex viewpoints. The individual steps are routine, but the packaging as the 'infrastructure analytique' of the structure at infinity seems unpublished.
transcription_corrections: Indices throughout are d, d', d'', δ (Latin d and Greek delta), not α, α', α''.
In (164) the condition is 'd > δ', and in (165) it is 'si d > d' > d''', not '≠'.
Line 2: 'les morphismes D_J → D_{J'}' rather than 'D_γ → D_γ'.
'le rôle de "multiplicité des flèches"' (likely, after a struck word), not 'multiplicité des fibres'.
'entre éléments de sous-multiplicités à l'∞ associées à D' (the inserted word reads 'à l'∞' or similar), rather than 'du ×'.
The role assigned to D_{d,δ} → D_d is probably 'morphismes revêtements' (coverings), not 'morphismes normal'.
